app.title: Munimentum
pill.token.tip: Access to your Microsoft 365 account. Technically: an access token from the Graph Explorer. Click to paste or renew it.
pill.ollama.tip.on: Meaning-based search and the summary are ready. They run through Ollama on this machine — nothing goes out. Click for the settings.
pill.ollama.tip.aus: Ollama is switched off in Settings. Search and export keep working; meaning-based search and the summary are absent. Click to go to the setting.
pill.ollama.tip.weg: Ollama does not answer at the address set. Text search and export keep working. Click for the settings, where each field says what is wrong.
pill.ollama.tip.modell: Ollama is running, but the embedding model is not loaded. Click for the settings, where each field says what is missing.
pill.mcp.tip.on: MCP access is available: the HTTP endpoint is running, and clients that start the server themselves (stdio) can reach it anyway. Click for the settings.
pill.mcp.tip.off: Only the HTTP endpoint is not running. A client that starts the server itself (stdio) — which is how Claude Desktop does it — still has access. Click for the settings.
pill.mcp.tip.aus: MCP access is switched off entirely: the server refuses to serve, over stdio as well as HTTP. Click for the settings.
export.what.sub: Your selection is saved and also applies to the schedule. Every run fetches only what is new — a second run is quick. The (i) on a source says what is chosen and when it last ran; the gear leads to its settings.
export.channels.note: Channels bring along the archives of whole teams – that grows very large, fast. Meant for the exceptional case, not for every run.
log.title: Log
search.sub.none: There is no index yet. Export and index first.
search.date.bad: The date marked in red does not exist — please correct it. Nothing was searched; otherwise that limit would silently have been missing.
search.date.turned: “from” is after “to” — nothing can lie between them.
search.person.none: Nobody by that name in the archive.
search.person.more: … and {n} more — type a little further.
files.none: No mirrored files in the index yet – export OneDrive or SharePoint first, then index.
search.gone.note: Shows only messages that are no longer in the mailbox — they are still here in the archive. This is detected during export: anything that used to be there and is now missing is checked with Microsoft. Do not rely on it blindly: Exchange assigns a new id when a message is moved, so it can no longer be found under the old one — a message that was merely moved can show up here too.
search.thread.alone: No further messages in this conversation.
cal.stats: {n} appointments in the calendar export · {r} reconstructed from mail · as of {when}
cal.st.deleted: Deleted — reconstructed from a cancellation mail
cal.st.gone: No longer in the calendar — reconstructed from mail
cal.rb.note: Appointments that are no longer in the calendar export and were recovered from invitation, reply or cancellation mails alone. “Deleted” means a cancellation mail exists. Click opens the source mail.
cal.rb.empty: No reconstructed appointments — the mailbox held no matching invitation or cancellation mails.
cal.rb.off: Recovering deleted appointments is switched off — turn it on in the settings under “Outlook export”.
cal.missing: Calendar data is missing — start “Build calendar & contacts” under Settings → Expert mode.
book.f.note: “From contacts” are the entries of your Outlook address book — with company and phone number. “From communication” are senders and recipients found in the archive: more complete, but without master data. Anyone in both appears once.
settings.cadence.i: How often this source is synced at most – applies to scheduled AND manual runs. Below its interval it is skipped with a clear log line; “always” is the default.
settings.cadence.cat.i: How often this part is synced at most – for scheduled and manual runs alike. While the last clean run is still within the interval, the run skips it with a line in the log.
settings.cadence.overrides.mail.i: A folder may depart from the sync cadence above; everything below inherits its value until a deeper folder sets its own. “Pick folders…” shows the folder tree of the last sync; here a value can be changed or removed with ×.
settings.cadence.overrides.teams.i: A team, a channel or a chat may depart from the cadence of its kind; a value on a team applies to all its channels until a channel sets its own. “Pick teams and chats…” shows the list of the last sync; here a value can be changed or removed with ×.
settings.cadence.overrides.none: No departures – everything follows the cadence above.
settings.cadence.overrides.onedrive.i: A folder may depart from the sync cadence above; everything below inherits its value until a deeper folder sets its own. The drive is still listed in one go – files in a folder not yet due wait and are fetched once it is.
settings.cadence.overrides.todo.i: A list may depart from the sync cadence above. “Pick lists…” shows the lists of the last sync; here a value can be changed or removed with ×.
settings.cadence.overrides.sharepoint.i: A folder inside a library may depart from the cadence of its URL row; everything below inherits its value until a deeper folder sets its own. The library is still listed in one go – files in a folder not yet due wait until it is.
kadenz.title.teams: Sync cadence per team and chat
kadenz.info.mail: A value applies to the folder and everything below it until a deeper folder sets its own. “As above” is the cadence from the block, in brackets the folder it comes from. Folders the rules leave out have no cadence.
kadenz.info.teams: Four roots, one per kind, with the cadence from the block. A value on a team applies to all its channels, a value on a channel or chat only to that one. What the rules leave out has no cadence.
kadenz.info.onedrive: A value applies to the folder and everything below it until a deeper folder sets its own. The drive is listed in one go; files in a folder not yet due wait until it is. Folders the rules leave out have no cadence.
kadenz.info.todo: Every list may have its own cadence; “as above” is the one from the block. Lists the rules leave out have no cadence.
kadenz.info.sharepoint: The libraries per site, the folders below. A library carries the cadence of its URL row; a value on a folder applies to it and everything below until a deeper folder sets its own. Folders the rules leave out have no cadence.
kadenz.count: {n} set · become rows in the block, saved with “Save settings”
cadence.units.none: No URLs yet – add one with +.
sched.title: Export regularly
sched.onedrive.i: Only when OneDrive is ticked under “Build archive” – this toggle narrows the scheduled run, it does not switch the source on.
sched.sharepoint.i: Only when SharePoint is ticked under “Build archive” and URLs are configured – this toggle narrows the scheduled run, it does not switch the source on.
sched.pages.i: Only when pages are ticked under “Build archive” and URLs are configured – this toggle narrows the scheduled run, it does not switch the source on.

settings.teams.title: Teams
settings.embed_images: Embed inline images in the HTML
settings.refresh_channels: Check channels for new replies on every run
settings.skip_empty_chats: Skip chats without a real message
settings.outlook.title: Outlook
settings.skip_folders.sub: Folders the default selection leaves out (one per line, case does not matter). Empty = export every folder.
settings.speed.title: Speed
settings.mcp_autostart: Start the HTTP endpoint with the app
settings.datadir.restart: Saved. Takes effect after restarting the app.
settings.datadir.same: That is already the current folder.
settings.lang.title: Language
settings.saved: Saved — applies to the next run.
wizard.token.title: Access to your Microsoft 365 account
wizard.auth.token.hint: No need to involve IT. Lasts a few hours, then paste a new one.
wizard.auth.login.hint: Sign in once, and the schedule keeps running unattended.
wizard.token.intro: The app never signs you in itself: you pick up an access key from Microsoft and paste it here. It lasts a few hours — how long is set by your company. The key stays on this computer, readable only by you, and goes to nobody but Microsoft.
wizard.token.none: No access yet — without it nothing can be exported.
wizard.token.expired: The access has expired. Please pick up a fresh key.
wizard.token.missing: This access is still missing permissions: {list}. A wider one counts — if you have Mail.ReadWrite you do not need Mail.Read as well.
wizard.token.step1: Open the Graph Explorer — Microsoft's test page. Sign in there with your work account, top right.
wizard.token.step2: Switch to the Access token tab and copy the long text in full.
wizard.token.scopes.title: What the app is allowed to read
wizard.token.scopes.intro: The first time, Microsoft asks for your consent: tab Modify permissions, then Consent. Usually this is long since done.
wizard.token.scopes.note: That tab only lists permissions for the request currently in the address bar. If one is not offered, put the matching query in there, run it, and look again.
wizard.login.intro: You sign in with Microsoft once. Afterwards the app only keeps permission to issue itself new keys — it never sees your password. That permission stays on this computer, readable only by you; “Sign out” deletes it.
wizard.login.code.intro: Open {url} and enter this code:
wizard.login.waiting: This window will say so by itself once it worked.
wizard.login.own.title: Use your own app registration
wizard.login.own.intro: With nothing entered, the app uses Microsoft's own application Graph Command Line Tools, which is pre-approved in almost every tenant. If your company requires its own registration, put its values here.
wizard.ollama.title: Set up Ollama (optional)
wizard.ollama.intro: Ollama computes the embeddings for semantic search. Everything runs locally, nothing leaves your machine.
wizard.ollama.off: Ollama is not running. Without it there is no semantic search — export, full-text search and MCP still work.
wizard.ollama.nomodel: Ollama is running, but the model {model} is still missing.
wizard.ollama.wait: Once that finishes this window will say so by itself — or click “Check again”
wizard.ollama.without: Continue without Ollama — full-text index only
wizard.ollama.without.note: “Continue without Ollama” builds a pure full-text index (BM25). Search and MCP work with it immediately; the semantic half can be added later at any time.
wizard.ollama.ready.title: Ollama is ready
wizard.ollama.ready: Ollama is running and the model {model} is there. The next index gets embeddings and search becomes hybrid.
wizard.ollama.step.mac1: Download Ollama from {url} and drag it into Applications
wizard.ollama.step.mac2: Start Ollama once (icon in the menu bar)
wizard.ollama.step.win1: Download OllamaSetup.exe from {url} and run it
wizard.ollama.step.win2: Ollama then starts automatically in the background
srv.job.token: Access token expired – paste a fresh key in the app or sign in.
srv.job.skipped: Skipped: {step} — the export brought nothing new.
srv.job.cancel: Cancellation requested — the running step is being stopped.
srv.token.found: Access found for {account}, valid for another {rest}.
srv.token.scopes: Missing permissions: {list} — click the access pill above.
srv.token.none: No access stored — the assistant walks you through it.
srv.token.expired: The stored access has expired — the assistant is opening.
srv.token.saved.scopes: Still missing permissions: {list} — consent at Microsoft and copy it again.
srv.token.short: That does not look like an access key.
srv.token.stale: That key has already expired — please copy a fresh one.
srv.login.ok: Signed in — the schedule can now run unattended.
srv.logout: Signed out — the stored permission was deleted.
srv.datadir.set: Data folder from the next start: {path}
srv.indexdir.set: Index folder from the next start: {path}
srv.layout.kept: Existing archive in the flat layout found – data and index stay there ({data}), nothing was moved. Splitting storage is possible, not required: quit the app, move the folders yourself, set the paths in the settings.
srv.layout.movefail: The archive could not move into {path}: {detail}. It keeps running where it lies for now; the next start tries again – close programs that hold the index open first (Claude Desktop's MCP server, for one).
srv.layout.moved: Your archive now lives in {path} – renamed as a whole, nothing copied, nothing else changed; data or index paths you set outside the app folder still apply. Claude Desktop: copy the MCP snippet again, its paths have changed.
srv.layout.noindex: The configured index folder holds no index ({index}) – run an index, or point the index folder to where the index is.
srv.datadir.unwritable: This folder cannot be written to: {detail}
srv.datadir.shared: Profile “{profile}” already uses this folder. Two profiles in one data or index folder mix their archives – choose a folder of its own.
srv.profile.created: Profile “{name}” created – empty until it is opened and set up for the first time.
srv.profile.badname: A profile name consists of lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 32 characters.
srv.profile.createfail: The profile folder could not be created: {detail}
srv.profile.active: Profile “{name}” is open right now – here or in a second instance – switch or close it first.
srv.profile.impossible: With a fixed data folder (--data-dir) there are no profiles – nor while the archive has not moved into profiles/ yet.
srv.mcp.noindex: No index available — MCP has nothing to serve.
srv.mcp.badaction: action must be start or stop.
srv.lexical.choice: Without embeddings by choice — the index is built as a pure full-text index (search without semantic hits).
srv.lexical.noollama: Ollama unavailable — the index is built as a pure full-text index (search without semantic hits).
srv.sched.notoken: Schedule skipped: no valid token — please paste a new one in the assistant.
srv.layout.pointer: The old data-folder pointer ({pointer}) names an archive in {data}. Since 7.0 it is no longer followed, and exports are blocked – otherwise a second archive would grow beside the real one. Please move app_config.json, gx_token.txt, msal_cache.bin and runs.db into {home}, then set the data folder to {data} in the settings and delete the pointer file.
srv.legacy.state: Old export state found ({stores}) – still in the pre-6.2 format. Runs are blocked, because otherwise everything would be fetched again and the deletion markers would be lost. Please run the latest 6.x release once, it moves the state over; 7.0 then carries on.
srv.notoken: No token stored — please go through the assistant.
srv.nostart: The job could not be started.
srv.nomcpmodule: mcp_server could not be loaded ({error}) — 'pip install -r requirements.txt'?
update.ahead: Newer than the latest release ({v}) — probably a pre-release.
update.ahead.banner: You are running version {v}; the latest published one is {latest}. This looks like a pre-release — it has not been through a release build. For everyday use, prefer a published version.
app.quit.tip: Quit – closes the application along with the schedule and the MCP server. Your exported data is kept.
quit.confirm: Quit the app? The MCP server goes with it, and search will no longer be reachable.
quit.confirm.busy: A job is running. Quitting cancels it — anything already exported is kept and the next run continues from there. Quit anyway?
quit.done: Stopped. You can close this window. To carry on, just start the app again.
search.ai.label: Summary by a local AI (Ollama) – source data in the list of results below
search.ai.note: This summary does not come from your archive but from an AI model running in Ollama on this machine. It is based solely on the results below — the bracketed numbers jump to them. A model this size errs more easily than Claude: when in doubt, read the result itself.
search.ai.err.model: Ollama does not know this model: {detail}. Check the settings or fetch it with “ollama pull”.
srv.answer.nomodel: Ollama has no model for the summary: {model}
srv.answer.noquery: Without a search term there is nothing to answer.
export.index.only.when: When you do not want to fetch anything new but rebuild the search index — for instance after pulling an embedding model in Ollama so that search can work semantically too.
export.calendar.build.when: Re-reads every mail to recover deleted appointments from them. It runs after each Outlook export anyway; separately only if calendar or contacts stay empty.
expert.title: Expert mode
expert.i: Not normally needed — “Start export” does everything in turn. This is where the individual steps live, for the cases the (i) next to each one names, and the description of the HTTP API.
expert.openapi.i: The complete HTTP API of this interface as an OpenAPI 3.1 file — for scripts that talk to the backend directly (127.0.0.1 only, no authentication; the app must be running).
run.index.analytics_failed: The overview could not be prepared ({error}) – it computes on demand instead.
run.folder_incomplete: {name} incomplete ({error}) – the next run continues there.
run.default_selection: No selection passed in – exporting the default selection.
run.workers_hint: Exchange allows 4 concurrent requests per mailbox – {n} workers mostly cause throttling.
run.resume_hint: {n} new so far – just start again, the run continues there.
run.folders_failed: {n} folders could not be listed completely – the next run fetches the rest.
run.state_unreadable: Progress file unreadable – starting without resume.
run.sync.changed: Changes: {new} new, {gone} no longer there, {renamed} renamed.
run.selection.empty: The rules select nothing – nothing to do.
run.selection.new: {n} new since the last sync – they follow the rules automatically.
run.folders.initial: No folder tree yet – loading it once (a few minutes for large mailboxes).
run.calendars.none: No calendars readable – the list is not stored.
run.gone.checking: Checking {n} mails that were no longer in the mailbox…
run.gone.healed: {n} earlier deletion markers withdrawn – the mails were only moved.
run.gone.deferred: {n} further candidates will be checked on the next run.
run.sharepoint.path_unmatched: SharePoint: the path “{path}” from {url} matches no library – the whole site comes along.
settings.pages.title: SharePoint pages
settings.pages.image_max.i: Images up to this size are embedded into the HTML files; larger ones stay links, otherwise the files balloon. 0 means: no limit, embed everything.
settings.sharepoint.pages.title: Which sites' pages get exported
settings.sharepoint.pages.i: One site URL per line – the modern site pages (news included) of the site and all its subsites are exported as standalone HTML. Text is kept, images are embedded, other web parts (lists, embeds) appear as named placeholders; classic wiki pages are not part of that API. The pages are full-text searchable afterwards.
run.pages.images_failed: Pages: {n} images could not be fetched – the original links remain.
run.rules_changed: {name}: selection changed – the folder is read once in full in this run.
run.outlook.delta_reset: {name}: change tracking restarted – the folder is read once in full.
run.outlook.folders_paced: {n} folders below their cadence – not in this run.
run.calendar.window: {name}: appointments from {from} on plus everything ahead.
run.teams.delta_reset: {name}: change tracking restarted – the channel is read once in full.
run.teams.paced: {name}: {n} conversations below their cadence – not in this run.
run.onedrive.folders_paced: {n} folders below their cadence – their files wait until then.
run.todo.paced: {n} lists below their cadence – not in this run.
run.sharepoint.folders_paced: {name}: {n} folders below their cadence – their files wait until then.
run.teams.delta_failed: {name}: change tracking unavailable ({error}) – the channel is read in full each run.
run.teams.excluded: {n} conversations left out by the rules or the start day.
run.teams.since_invalid: Start day “{value}” is not a date (YYYY-MM-DD) – ignored.
run.todo.delta_reset: {name}: change tracking restarted – the list is read once in full.
run.pages.none: No site URLs configured for the pages export – nothing to do.
run.sharepoint.denied: SharePoint access not granted ({url}) – skipping the site.
run.sharepoint.none: No SharePoint URLs configured – nothing to do.
run.teams.channels_failed: Channels of “{name}” could not be loaded ({error}).
run.teams.channels_denied: Channel access not granted – channels are skipped. {error}
run.teams.found: {n} teams found – all their channels come along.
run.teams.chats: {n} matching chats: {new} new, {updated} with new messages, {unchanged} unchanged.
run.teams.channels_check: {n} channels are being checked for changes.
run.teams.chats_skipped: No chat category selected – skipping chats.
run.drive.delta: Enumeration: only changes since the last run.
run.drive.full: Enumeration: full walk (first run or rebuild) – large libraries can take a while.
run.full_sync: Full sync: the stored change tracking is set aside – everything is read and written again, nothing in the archive is deleted.
run.drive.resync: Delta pointer expired – the library is re-enumerated in full once.
run.drive.retry: Because of the errors, the next run picks up what is missing – no new full walk needed.
run.drive.resume: Enumeration: resuming the interrupted walk – {n} entries already stored.
run.drive.replan: Enumeration already stored from the interrupted run – continuing straight with the downloads.
run.index.read: {reused} files unchanged and re-used, {read} read – {chunks} chunks ({s} s).
run.index.plan: {chunks} chunks: {reused} reused, {new} new ({short} too short to carry meaning).
run.index.saved_stale: {n} existing embeddings saved – a later run with Ollama reuses them.
run.index.rebuild: Old index unreadable – rebuilding from scratch.
run.index.no_pool: Reading without a process pool, one core only ({error}).
ana.title: What the archive holds
ana.sub: Computed once per index run — Microsoft is not asked for this.
ana.komm.title: Communication
ana.dateien.title: Files & space
ana.gone.files: Files no longer at the source
ana.gone.files.hint: Still here in the archive — only deleted at Microsoft.
ana.dateitypen.sub: What kind of files the mirrors hold.
ana.threads.hint: Related mails, recognised from their headers.
ana.attachments.hint: The names are searchable, the contents are not yet.
ana.files.hint: From the OneDrive and SharePoint mirrors. Name and folder are searchable, the contents are not yet.
ana.gone.hint: Still here in the archive — only deleted at Microsoft.
ana.gone.hint.klick: Still here in the archive — only deleted at Microsoft. Click to show them in search.
settings.runs_retention_months.i: How far back the run overview (Overview → Runs) reaches. Only counts, durations and switches are stored per run – locally in runs.db in the data folder. Older entries are removed on start and after every run.
settings.log_retention_days.i: Every run's log is stored in the run history (runs.db) and shown inline under Overview → Health. Lines older than this are dropped; the run rows themselves have their own retention above.
ana.runs.title: Runs
ana.runs.sub: Every run of the app, with duration and result per step.
ana.runs.empty: No runs recorded yet – the first one will appear here.
ana.runs.log.empty: No log stored for this run (any more) — the retention window in the settings decides how long lines are kept.
ana.check.title: Completeness
ana.check.sub: Compares what Microsoft counts per folder with what is here. Deleted messages do not count as a gap — they are still in the archive.
ana.check.skipped: Not counted: {n} mails in folders the selection leaves out ({ordner}). They are not missing — they were never fetched.
ana.check.skipped.files: Not counted: {n} files in folders the selection leaves out ({ordner}). They are not missing — they were never fetched.
folders.title: Which folders get exported
folders.none: No folder tree synced yet — the first export fetches it once.
folders.state: {an} of {gesamt} folders selected, {mails} mails. As of {when}.
folders.state.files: {an} of {gesamt} folders selected, {mails} files. As of {when}.
settings.onedrive.title: OneDrive
settings.onedrive.rules.title: Which folders get mirrored
plan.title: What gets exported
plan.stand: Folder tree as of {when}, evaluated with the rules currently in the box above.
plan.weg: Only in the archive: {n} folders, {mails} mails
export.sharepoint.nourls: No URLs configured yet – set what gets mirrored under Settings → SharePoint.
settings.sharepoint.title: SharePoint
settings.sharepoint.urls.title: Which sites get mirrored
settings.sharepoint.urls.i: One URL per line – a site or a library, copied straight from the browser. Each URL resolves to its document libraries and is mirrored like OneDrive: current version, deletions stay with a tombstone note. Access needs the Sites.Read.All permission.
settings.sharepoint.include.i: Comma-separated, e.g. “pdf, docx”. Empty means: every file type. Applies to mirror and size preview alike.
settings.sharepoint.exclude.i: Comma-separated, e.g. “mp4, iso”. Wins over “Only these extensions” on conflict.
settings.sharepoint.maxmb.i: Larger files are not mirrored and count as excluded. 0 means: no limit.
settings.sharepoint.rules.i: On top of the URL list and the extensions: the same rules as for OneDrive, on paths “<site>/<library>/<path>” as the export list shows them. Empty = every path. A changed rule reads the library once in full on the next run.
sharepoint.types.none: Nothing counted yet – the size preview also counts the file types.
sharepoint.preview.empty: Nothing found. The log says whether a site was unreachable or access is missing (the key needs Sites.Read.All).
sharepoint.preview.result: A run would fetch {n} files ({mb} MB); {skipped} filtered out. Details under Overview → Completeness.
settings.calendars.title: Calendars
settings.calendars.rules.i: The same rules as for mailbox folders, one per line, the last matching one wins: “- kalender/**” leaves all of them out, a “+ kalender/Privat” after it takes one back in. Empty means the default calendar only — a mailbox often carries birthdays, holidays and calendars other people shared, and nobody meant those. The list comes from the sync; new calendars follow the rules automatically.
settings.calendar_months_back.i: After the first export a run reads only this window: that many months back plus everything ahead. What was archived before stays. 0 = every appointment, every run. “Read the calendar in full” reads everything once, window or not.
settings.outlook_since.i: First export of a folder only: no mail older than this day. Empty = the whole history. Folders already exported are not affected.
settings.calendars.none: No calendar list synced yet — the first export fetches it once.
plan.an.cal: Exported: {n} calendars, {mails} appointments in the archive
plan.aus.cal: Left out: {n} calendars, {mails} appointments in the archive
plan.weg.cal: Only in the archive: {n} calendars, {mails} appointments
report.title: Report a problem
report.intro: Below is what would be reported. Read it, change whatever you like – “Open on GitHub” turns it into a draft that you get to see once more over there. You need a GitHub account for this.
report.field.title: Subject
report.privacy: E-mail addresses and user names in paths have already been replaced. Folder names and subject lines are beyond what a program can spot – they may still be in here. Please read through before you make this public.
report.cut: _(Log shortened – the full text did not fit into the address.)_
report.truncated: The report was too long for the address; older log lines are missing from the draft. Use “Copy” for the full text and paste it over there.
report.body.hint: What did you do, what did you expect, what happened instead?
settings.notifications.i: Reports the end of a run through the operating system’s notifications – even with the browser tab closed, e.g. when the schedule exports. “Errors only” reports failures and an expired access key, “All runs” every finish. Everything stays on this machine; currently macOS only, the system asks for permission once, and clicking the notification opens the interface in the browser.
srv.notify.failed: {label} failed – details are in the log.
srv.notify.token: Access key expired – sign in again in the app.
settings.userflow_actions.i: Remembers the last steps taken in the interface – only their kind (tab, search, run), never content such as search text or names. Kept only in the memory of the open page and gone when it closes; the app sends nothing. The list appears only in a bug report, where you review and edit it before sending. 0 switches recording off.
search.mode.needs: The two on the right need Ollama.
search.ph.text: Words that appear exactly like this
search.ph.ki: Ask a question about your archive
settings.export.title: Sources
settings.export.i: What comes along per source, and how. What gets fetched at all is chosen under “Build archive”.
settings.embed_images.i: Images end up inside the HTML file rather than as a link. Off: much smaller files, but the images are gone later.
settings.cache_images.i: Images already fetched are kept, so a repeat export does not download them again.
settings.refresh_channels.i: Channels are checked for changes every run: new posts via change tracking, replies on posts of the last two weeks every time, older posts once a week. Off: channels come once only, which is faster.
settings.skip_empty_chats.i: Chats consisting only of joins, calls and system messages are not created.
settings.include_hidden.i: Folders such as “Conversation History” that Outlook creates itself and normally hides.
settings.calendar_reconstruct.i: Reads every mail for invitations and cancellations and rebuilds appointments that are no longer in the calendar. The slowest step of a run.
folders.rules.i: One rule per line, the last matching one wins — the .gitignore idea. “- E-Mail/Archiv/**” leaves out, “+ E-Mail/Archiv/Wichtig/**” brings back.
settings.skip_folders.i: Folder names the default selection leaves out — trash, drafts, junk. Applies only while there are no rules above.
settings.onedrive.rules.i: The same mechanism as for the mailbox, on drive paths. The mirror holds the current state; anything deleted stays here and gets a marker.
settings.onedrive.maxmb.i: Skip large files. 0 means no limit.
settings.workers.i: How many requests go to Microsoft Graph at once. Graph allows no more than four per mailbox.
settings.mirror_workers.i: Applies to OneDrive and SharePoint. Unlike the mailbox, Microsoft documents no fixed limit here – throttling is budget-based, and the run then waits visibly (HTTP 429 in the log). 16 is the app's ceiling; lower the value if wait lines pile up.
sched.i: Repeats the export at a fixed interval while the app is open. With a pasted access key it ends when the key expires — unattended runs need signing in.
sched.enabled.i: While the app is open it repeats the chosen run.
sched.every.i: Time between two runs. Shorter than five minutes is not possible.
sched.outlook.i: Fetch mail, calendar and contacts — depending on the selection under “Build archive”.
sched.teams.i: Fetch chats and channels — depending on the selection under “Build archive”.
sched.index.i: Refresh the search index after the export. Without it the search will not find what is new.
sched.calendar.i: Rebuild calendar and address book. Needed when appointments or contacts are exported too.
settings.ollama.title: AI
settings.ollama.i: Meaning-based search and the summary need language models on this machine. They are currently run by Ollama — hence the name of the switch below. Without it, everything else works unchanged: export, text search, analytics.
settings.ollama.url.i: Where Ollama can be reached. Only change this if it runs on a different port or machine.
settings.ollama.folgen: Ollama will no longer be looked for; the dot in the navigation on the left says “off”. Search then knows only text search, the index only full text — and without vectors there is no “Find similar” either.
settings.index.title: Index
settings.index.i: The index makes the archive searchable and is built after every export. Without Ollama the full-text index remains — and that needs no settings.
settings.index.kind.i: Full text finds words that appear exactly like that — fast and without Ollama. Meaning additionally finds related wording, but costs time while building.
settings.index.parked: Existing vectors are set aside on the next run, not deleted — switching back needs no re-embedding.
settings.embed_model.i: Turns text into vectors. bge-m3 understands German and English. Changing it invalidates the existing index.
settings.batch.i: How many passages go to Ollama at once. Measured on a real archive, 128 is about a fifth faster than 64; Ollama rejects 256. Larger means fewer requests but more memory.
settings.semantic_min.i: Meaning-based search also finds what does not contain your words — “applied for leave” finds the mail about the time-off request. That needs a floor: without one it always returns its best hits, even when nothing fits. Narrow the search to a single day and you get every message of that day, sorted by similarity. 45 % is measured and the default: a nonsense query never got above 43 %, while real queries were still above 50 % at the fortieth hit. Higher (60–70 %) makes search strict — related hits disappear and short queries often return nothing. Lower (below 35 %) brings back the old behaviour: plenty of noise, especially together with filters. 0 turns it off. Above 80 % is almost always too much. Full-text search is unaffected — anything containing your words literally is still found. A different embedding model has different distances and needs a different setting.
settings.ki.title: AI answer
settings.ki.i: Condenses the hits of a search into one paragraph, with source references. Runs in your Ollama; nothing leaves the machine.
settings.chat_model.i: The language model that writes the summary. Larger models phrase better and need more memory.
settings.answer_sources.i: How many hits the summary takes into account. More means more complete, but slower.
mcp.i: A small server through which MCP clients such as Claude can search and read this archive themselves. It binds to 127.0.0.1 only and has no authentication — it does not belong on a network.
settings.mcp_port.i: Which port the MCP server listens on. A changed port takes effect after restarting the server.
settings.mcp_autostart.i: The HTTP endpoint then runs as soon as the app runs. It covers that one route only: clients that launch the server themselves as a subprocess (stdio) do not need it and run independently.
settings.app.title: App
settings.app.i: Where the data lives, what language the interface speaks, and which version is running.
settings.datadir.i: All exports live here. Empty means: data/ inside the profile folder. A change moves nothing — move the folder yourself, then point here; takes effect after a restart.
settings.indexdir.i: The search index (rag_store) — hot, random-access reads: put it on a fast disk. Empty means: inside the profile folder. A change moves nothing — move the folder yourself, then point here; takes effect after a restart.
settings.homedir.i: Settings, access token and run history of this profile live here: profiles/<name>/ in the app folder. This place is fixed — only the data and index folders above can point elsewhere.
settings.appdir.i: Where the application itself runs from. It never holds any of your data.
settings.search_results.i: How many hits one page of search results shows. More means less paging.
settings.analytics_skip: People to leave out of the overview
settings.analytics_skip.i: One per line, spelled as it appears in the overview — usually your own name. They no longer show up under “who you exchanged the most with”: your own messages otherwise sit far at the top and say nothing about the exchange with others. The whole name is compared, ignoring case; if you appear under several spellings, add each. Export and search are unaffected.
settings.filetype_hidden.i: Comma-separated, e.g. “p7s, asc”. These types do not appear in the file type filter — otherwise the list fills up with what mail programs attach by themselves: signature blocks, encryption envelopes. Display only: everything is still exported and still findable, and a mail like that is still found by its attachment name.
settings.lang.i: Applies to this interface. Exported content is never touched.
update.enabled.i: Asks api.github.com once at startup whether a newer version exists. Otherwise the app talks to nothing but Microsoft Graph and your local Ollama.
search.mode.off: Ollama is switched off — only text search is available.
ana.verlauf.sub: Messages per month, stacked by source. A missing column is a month without a single message.
ana.luecken: {n} gap(s) in the archive: {liste}. Within the period that otherwise holds messages — before the first and after the last there is nothing to miss.
ana.luecken.keine: No gaps: every month between the first and the last message holds something.
ana.wachstum.sub: How the archive grew over time, cumulative.
ana.typen.sub: Which file types are attached to mail in the archive.
ana.dateien.sub: What takes up the room — one group chat can reach hundreds of megabytes.
ana.personen.sub: Who you exchanged the most messages with.
search.menu.similar.aus: Needs an index built with meaning — this one is full text only.
settings.mcp_enabled.i: The hard switch. Off means the server refuses to serve, no matter who starts it — the HTTP endpoint here as well as a client that launches it as a subprocess (stdio, which is how Claude Desktop does it). The entry you pasted into your client stays valid and works again the moment you allow it here; there is nothing to delete. This is a safeguard against accident, not an access barrier: anyone who reaches this machine can flip it.
srv.mcp.disabled: MCP access is switched off — allow it in Settings first.
sched.planner.i: Include the Planner boards in scheduled runs. Only narrows: the checkbox under “Build archive” must be on anyway.
settings.planner.title: Planner
settings.planner.urls.title: Board URLs
settings.planner.urls.i: One Planner board per row – paste the board's address from the browser (new or classic Planner). Each row has its own sync cadence; comments come along, legacy and chat-based alike. Reading needs Tasks.Read plus Group.Read.All for the legacy comments; the token wizard lists both.
settings.planner.attachments.i: Tasks reference files that live in the board's own SharePoint library – one that is usually not mirrored on its own. Switched on, the export downloads every referenced file next to the board and the cards link the local copy; kept current by change tag. Needs the Files.Read.All permission; the token wizard lists it.
settings.planner_sweep_hours.i: Chat comments carry no change signal, so the export re-reads them for every task at this interval (one request per task). 0 = never; “Sync now” no longer forces it.
settings.planner.legacy.i: Planner has taken no legacy comments from the group conversation since February 2026 – after a board's first export they are no longer checked. This run reads them once more for every board, in case someone still replied from Outlook.
ana.planner.hint: Boards with descriptions, checklists and comments – full-text searchable.
run.planner.bad_url: Planner: no plan id in {url} – paste the board address from the browser.
run.planner.comments_failed: {name}: group conversation not readable ({error}) – legacy comments stay as they were.
run.planner.names_failed: {n} names not resolved ({error}) – the cards show ids; the next run asks again.
run.planner.ref_failed: Attachment of “{name}” not fetched ({error}) – the card keeps the online link.
run.planner.threads: {name}: checking the group conversation for comment changes…
run.planner.legacy_skip: {name}: legacy comments stay as they were on the first export – Planner takes no new ones; read them again under Settings → Planner if needed.
run.planner.none: No board URLs configured for the Planner export – nothing to do.
sched.todo.i: Include the To Do lists in scheduled runs. Only narrows: the checkbox under “Build archive” must be on anyway.
sched.onenote.i: Include the OneNote notebooks in scheduled runs. Only narrows: the checkbox under “Build archive” must be on anyway.
settings.todo.title: To Do
settings.todo.rules.i: The same rules as for mailbox folders, one per line, the last match wins – on the list names. “Sync lists” fetches the names, “Show export list” shows what the rules mean. Empty = every list the account sees: own, shared and the built-in ones.
settings.todo.none: No lists synced yet — the first export fetches them once.
settings.onenote.title: OneNote
settings.onenote.rules.i: The same rules as for mailbox folders, one per line, the last matching one wins: “- **” leaves all of them out, a “+ Projekte” after it takes one back in; the name is the notebook's folder as the export list shows it. Empty means every notebook. The list comes from the sync; new notebooks follow the rules automatically.
settings.onenote.none: No notebook list synced yet — the first export fetches it once.
settings.onenote.cadence.i: How often each notebook is synced at most – applies to scheduled and manual runs; below its interval it is skipped with a clear log line. “Sync now” runs exactly that one notebook immediately, cadence ignored. Notebooks the rules leave out are listed greyed.
settings.onenote.cadence.none: No notebooks known yet – sync the list first.
plan.an.nb: Exported: {n} notebooks, {mails} pages in the archive
plan.aus.nb: Left out: {n} notebooks, {mails} pages in the archive
plan.weg.nb: Only in the archive: {n} notebooks, {mails} pages
plan.aus.teams: Left out: {n} conversations, {mails} in the archive
plan.weg.teams: Only in the archive: {n} conversations, {mails} files
plan.an.todo: Exported: {n} lists, {mails} tasks in the archive
plan.aus.todo: Left out: {n} lists, {mails} tasks in the archive
plan.weg.todo: Only in the archive: {n} lists, {mails} tasks
settings.onenote.note: Every notebook the account sees can come along – own and shared ones; which do is a matter of the rules below. One folder per notebook, the section groups and sections below it, one HTML per page with its images and attachments, so it opens offline. Only pages that changed are fetched again; a page that leaves its section keeps its file and gets a marker. Needs Notes.Read; the token wizard lists it. OneNote allows 400 requests an hour; a large notebook therefore takes several runs, each continuing where the last one stopped.
settings.onenote.image_max.i: Images up to this size are embedded into the page file; larger ones and every file attachment land in a folder next to the page, linked from it. 0 means: embed every image.
settings.teams.attachments.i: A file shared in a chat or a channel post is only a link to the sender's OneDrive or the team's library – dead once the access ends. Switched on, the export fetches every such file next to its conversation (Anhaenge/…) and the HTML links the local copy; kept current by change tag. Needs the Files.Read.All permission; the token wizard lists it.
settings.teams.channel_files.i: The Files tab of every exported channel, mirrored like a SharePoint library: one walk per team library, the current version of every file, deleted ones with a tombstone (channels/<team>/Dateien/…). Channel posts then link into the mirror instead of fetching the file twice. Needs the Files.Read.All permission; the token wizard lists it.
settings.teams.files_max.i: Applies to both file switches. 0 means no limit.
settings.teams.rules: Which chats and channels are exported
settings.teams.rules.i: The same rules as for mailbox folders, one per line, the last match wins. Paths: “1on1/<title>”, “group/<title>”, “meeting/<title>”, “channels/<team>/<channel>” – “Sync team list” fetches the names, “Show export list” shows what the rules mean. Empty = everything in the ticked categories.
settings.teams.files.title: Files
settings.teams.none: No team list synced yet — the first export fetches it once.
settings.teams_since.i: First export of a conversation only: no message older than this day. Empty = the whole history. Conversations already exported are not affected.
ana.todo.hint: Lists with notes, steps and linked resources – full-text searchable.
ana.onenote.hint: Notebooks page by page – full-text searchable.
run.todo.attachment_failed: Attachment of “{name}” not fetched ({error}) – the card keeps its name.
run.todo.none: No To Do lists found – nothing to do.
run.onenote.section_failed: {name}: section not listed ({error}) – nothing counts as gone this run.
run.onenote.resources_failed: {name}: {n} images or attachments did not come – the page keeps their online links.
run.onenote.none: No OneNote notebooks found – nothing to do.
run.onenote.budget: OneNote allows 400 requests an hour – {name}: {n} pages wait for the next run, which continues here.
run.onenote.budget_rest: {n} notebooks wait for the next run as well.
run.onenote.throttled: OneNote keeps refusing (429): the hour's requests are spent – {name} continues with the next run.
run.teams.file_failed: File “{name}” not fetched ({error}) – the message keeps the online link.
stand.title: Your archive is current as of {when}
stand.step1.sub: Paste an access key from the Graph Explorer (valid for a few hours) or sign in once (then the schedule runs on its own).
stand.step2.sub: Tap below what should come along. Nothing is preselected: each source can mean tens of thousands of items.
stand.step3.sub: The first run fetches everything, every further one only what is new. Then the search is ready.
settings.storage.title: Profiles
settings.storage.i: A profile is an archive of its own: own access, own rules, own index, own folder under profiles/ in the app folder. All profiles above, the current one's folders below. Changing a path moves nothing — you move the data yourself.
settings.profile.switch.title: Switch profile
settings.profile.switch.i: The app restarts with the chosen profile; this page then reloads by itself. A running export has to finish first.
settings.profile.create.title: New profile
settings.profile.create.i: A name of lowercase letters, digits and dashes – not an e-mail address, the name lands in paths and in the MCP snippet. The new profile starts empty, with the first start: access, sources, archive.
settings.profile.rename.i: The folder under profiles/ gets the new name; paths inside it follow, paths elsewhere stay. Only for a profile that is not open right now – the open one after a switch. An MCP snippet of this profile carries the old name and has to be copied again.
settings.profile.rename.title: Rename profile
settings.profile.name: Name
settings.profile.noask.i: On: the start opens the last opened profile right away. Off: with more than one profile the app first asks which archive it should be.
profile.title: Which archive?
profile.sub: Every profile is an archive of its own: own access, own rules, own index, own folder. Nothing of it mixes.
profile.empty: empty – the first start walks you through three steps
profile.noask: Next time, open the last opened profile without asking
profile.settings.tip: Profile settings: all profiles, rename, create, folders
profile.pill.tip: Which archive is open right now – click to switch
profile.notback: The app has not answered – please open {url} by hand.
settings.sources.sub: Per source the essentials, the rest under “Advanced”. The gear on a source card leads straight here.
settings.full_sync.i: Reads this source again as on its first export: every stored change pointer is set aside, everything is fetched and written over – attachments and files included, so a setting changed later reaches what is already archived. Nothing in the archive is deleted; what Microsoft no longer has stays. It costs a first export and starts at once.
settings.full_sync.confirm: Read {source} again in full? Everything is fetched and written over as on the first export – that can take just as long. Nothing in the archive is deleted.
run.onenote.budget_wait: OneNote allows 400 requests an hour – this hour is spent, {name} continues with the next run.
run.paced_wait: Per-minute allowance reached – next request in {s} s.
lauf.title: Updating the archive
lauf.sub: Step {i} of {n} · running since {when} · The window stays open until the run is done.
lauf.minimize.note: Minimised, the run moves into the header – you can search meanwhile.
tour.title: Tour
tour.start: Tour: how to click your way through archive and search
tour.suche.later: Search comes after the first run
tour.suche.later.t: Once the first run is through there is something to search – the run window then offers you this tour.
tour.archiv.zugang.t: The frame at the top right shows whether Munimentum may read right now. A click opens the assistant: paste a key or sign in – both stay on this machine.
tour.archiv.quellen: Choose what goes into the archive
tour.archiv.quellen.t: Every card is a source, every chip a category: on or off. Nothing is preselected, because any category can mean tens of thousands of items.
tour.archiv.info: The (i) tells you where things stand
tour.archiv.info.t: What is chosen, how many folders, when it last ran – everything this source has to say about itself sits here, not on the page.
tour.archiv.zahnrad: The gear leads to the rules
tour.archiv.zahnrad.t: Which folders, how often, with which exceptions – you decide that in the source's settings. The button next to this one walks you through them.
tour.archiv.lauf.t: The first run fetches everything chosen, every later one only what changed since. Deleted items stay in the archive and get a marker.
tour.archiv.fenster.t: Progress, steps and the log of a run. “Minimise” moves it into the header, searching goes on meanwhile; a click on the pill brings it back.
tour.suche.feld: One field, three ways to search
tour.suche.feld.t: Text finds the words that actually occur. Similar finds related wording, AI answer sums up with sources – those two need Ollama.
tour.suche.filter.t: Person, source, date range, folder, file type: a set filter lights up where it stands. Nothing searches on its own – only “Search” or Enter does.
tour.suche.sichten: Four views onto the same archive
tour.suche.sichten.t: Hits, the calendar with appointments recovered from invitations, the address book, and a file browser over the mirrored drives.
tour.suche.treffer: A hit opens on the right
tour.suche.treffer.t: With its origin, the original, the whole conversation, “Find similar” and one click to everything with that person.
tour.suche.zeitplan: So it keeps going by itself
tour.suche.zeitplan.t: The schedule repeats the run while the app is open – one toggle per source. Each source also has its own sync cadence.
tour.suche.claude.t: The built-in MCP server hands the archive to Claude, on this machine only. The snippet for your client is here.
tour.quelle.block.t: The header line sums it up: how many folders, when last. Opened, the essential fields lie open, the rare ones under “Advanced”.
tour.quelle.regeln.t: One rule per line like in a .gitignore: “-” leaves out, “+” brings back what lies below, the last match wins. “Sync folder structure” fetches the folder list once; “Show export list” then shows what the rules mean – check before you save.
tour.quelle.kalender.t: Own rules, own list, own export list. Without a rule only your own calendar comes along. “Read the calendar in full” reads everything once, window or not.
tour.quelle.fenster.t: After the first export a run reads only this window: that many months back plus everything ahead. What was archived before stays.
tour.quelle.kadenz.t: Always, daily, weekly or monthly – per category, for scheduled and manual runs. Below the interval the run reports the skip in the log.
tour.quelle.abweichend.t: The cadence above applies to everything; a folder may depart, everything below inherits its value. “Pick folders…” opens the tree: drill in, one select per folder, “Apply” writes the rows here.
tour.quelle.erweitert.t: A start day for the first export, hidden folders, the default exclusions. Every row has its (i) saying what changes.
tour.quelle.speichern.t: The bar at the bottom appears only with unsaved changes: “Save settings” or “Discard”. Teams, OneDrive and To Do share these building blocks; SharePoint, Planner and OneNote have a table instead of rules: URL, cadence, “Sync now”.
lauf.done.title: Done – {n} new in {dauer}
lauf.failed.title: Did not finish: {detail}
